explainBack.prompt: Why might my chat app still ignore the photo I upload, even though DeepSeek released V4.1-Flash with native image understanding two days ago?
explainBack.response: Because the model is only one layer. Your app's maker decides which model sits behind the interface and whether the app forwards your image to it. If the maker hasn't connected V4.1-Flash, or connects it but never passes the picture along in the request, the model never receives the image — so nothing changes for you regardless of DeepSeek's announcement.
explainBack.expectedEvidence: A correct answer must use the article's causal chain: capability lives in the model (P002), the app maker chooses the connection and must pass the image (P003), and the app's own update is the authoritative signal of what you actually get.
explainBack.assessment: The article supports this answer fully in ordinary language; a reader relying only on P002–P003 can reconstruct every causal step without gaps.

unseenTransfer.prompt: Using only the article's mechanism, what most likely happened, and how could a user check whether the app can now understand photographed receipts?
unseenTransfer.response: Most likely nothing at the app changed: from September 14, requests sent under the older deepseek-v4-pro label are scheduled to route to V4.1-Flash until V4.1-Pro launches, so the model behind the unchanged interface was swapped upstream. Whether receipts-as-photos now work is a separate question — the app must accept an image and pass it to the model; the user should check whether the app offers image upload and what its own release notes claim, rather than assuming the routing switch added a visible feature.
unseenTransfer.expectedEvidence: Applies P004's label routing to explain the silent behaviour change and P003's connect-and-pass-along mechanism to separate upstream capability from app-level availability.
unseenTransfer.assessment: The article's mechanism resolves this novel scenario completely; both the routing note and the interface/model layering carry over without new assumptions, confirming genuine transfer.

One technical change arrives September 14: requests sent under the older deepseek-v4-pro label are scheduled to route to V4.1-Flash until V4.1-Pro launches. For everyday use, the useful question is simpler: can this specific app accept my picture, and what does it say it can do with it?
